description: CAPABILITY CLASS -> CONCRETE MODEL, per provider. A capability class says how much and what kind of reasoning a task needs; a provider entry says which model currently satisfies it there. Five classes, and the class is the whole vocabulary a user sees — in this file, in routing/profiles.json and in bin/fabric-model; which harness tier alias a class rides is the Claude Code adapter's business (runtime/claude-code/aliases.json), never named here. Compatibility shims (routing/shims.json) are a separate dimension keyed on the model family, and the composite `model@preset/slug` string is derived at runtime by tools/fabric/routing.py — it is never written here.

code-low.title: Inexpensive, mechanical delegated coding work
code-low.description: Simple repository exploration, routine modifications, test generation, documentation updates, lint fixes, and other low-risk tasks.

code-medium.title: Default delegated coding worker
code-medium.description: Normal engineering work that needs solid reasoning but is not unusually difficult or high-consequence.

code-high.title: Difficult or high-consequence engineering work
code-high.description: Architecture, difficult debugging, security review, subtle refactoring, concurrency, protocol design, and important cross-component reasoning.

code-plan.title: Planning and design reasoning
code-plan.description: The top reasoning tier for work whose output is a plan, a design or a judgement rather than an edit: shaping an implementation across components, weighing architectural trade-offs, reading a large change for what it means. The session itself can run on it (a profile's session may name any class).

code-review.title: The review class
code-review.description: The adversarial blind reviewer (the code-review agent) — the review of every PR, not a stand-in for another reviewer. Not a coding class: its model is gated by routing/policies/review-grade.json — chosen there by architect-cto, never by a profile layer alone — and reaches the reviewer through its agent file rather than a tier export, so it never shares an export with code-plan on the tier they both ride (runtime/claude-code/aliases.json).

anthropic.description: Plain `claude`, Anthropic by construction. A value is a native Claude id (claude-…) that pins the class — the launcher (`runtime/openrouter/launch --provider anthropic`) exports it for the tier the class rides, so the fabric decides the model rather than the harness's week — or null: the harness's own current model of that tier. code-low and code-medium are Sonnet 5.5 (the owner, 2026-09-29; read back in docs/live-checks/2026-09-29-sonnet-5-5.md); the upper classes and the review class are Opus 5.5 (the owner, 2026-09-25). Until 2026-09-25 each class had the top model of its own tier — Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 — and the review class claude-opus-5[1m] (architect-cto, 2026-09-15). The tier aliases stay as they are: they are how this harness spells a class; haiku and sonnet bind to Sonnet 5.5, opus and fable to Opus 5.5. The review pin reaches the reviewer's agent file rather than the fable export and is gated by routing/policies/review-grade.json like every other review model. No shim applies to a native Claude model.

openrouter.description: The broker path (runtime/openrouter/launch via the ori CLI). Values are OpenRouter model ids; the launcher derives the composite with the family shim and exports it for the tier the class rides (runtime/claude-code/aliases.json). The review class is not exported: its composite reaches the reviewer's agent file, gated by routing/policies/review-grade.json.
